$comment: THE MEASURED NUMBERS. Nothing in this file is estimated. A cell with no entry in `cells` renders as 'pending' — that is the correct state until a real run lands. See web/README.md for how to fill it in.
headline: PROVEN, from four retained artefacts anyone can re-count: the RLM mechanism runs. RLM-on issues `python` calls and never a shell call (82, 123); RLM-off issues shell calls and never `python` (114, 117). Four for four. NOT PROVEN, and now actively disconfirmed on the one task we probed hardest: that it performs better. That comparison started at 2/2 vs 0/2 and weakened at every repetition — 3/4 vs 1/4, then 4/5 vs 1/5, then 4/5 vs 2/6, then 4/6 vs 2/6 at p = 0.567. It is a coin flip. On DeepSWE (n = 2) chutescoder scores 1 of 2 and vanilla Codex scores 1 of 2, the same two tasks pass for pass; upstream Prime Agent scores 0 of 2. So: we match Codex, we beat the reference implementation of the idea we ported, we can prove the idea is running, and we cannot yet show it helps. Two earlier retractions and the reference-solution leak (faults 16-18) still stand below.

arms.label: Arm A — raw API
arms.desc: bench-runner calls the model directly, no agent loop. Exists only to reproduce the published numbers and prove our pipeline is calibrated.

arms.label: Arm B — vanilla Codex
arms.desc: upstream `codex exec`, pointed at Chutes. The conventional fixed-tool-schema harness baseline.

arms.label: Arm C — chutescoder
arms.desc: our fork, RLM mode on. Same binary as arm B, one flag different.

arms.label: Arm D — Prime Agent (upstream)
arms.desc: Prime Intellect's own agent, upstream 0.7.0, unmodified. The reference implementation of the idea chutescoder ports into Codex.

models.label: GLM-5.2
models.blocked_reason: Availability probing put zai-org/GLM-5.2-TEE far below both other models on the same probes (exact counts in the evidence line below, computed from the log rather than typed here). The successes it did record were one-token health checks; every multi-turn agent attempt returned `429 Infrastructure is at maximum capacity`. The cause looks structural rather than transient — the chute has 2 instances, one of them inactive, against Kimi K3's 7. Recorded as blocked: we did not quietly substitute another model.
blocked_caveats: The probe window ends roughly 75 minutes before the runs it is being used to explain, so there is no availability evidence covering the period when work actually happened. Roughly a third of attempts succeeding is bad, not impossible.

zai-org/GLM-5.1-TEE was available on every single probe and was never tried. It is a different model from the one the plan asks for, so it is not a substitute — but running it would have been the cheapest way to turn 'one model' into 'two models', and that was not done.

models.label: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.note: Used instead of a Chutes-hosted model to spare Chutes capacity while Kimi K3 was loaded. Provider recorded per run; not a silent substitution.

benchmarks.label: DeepSWE
benchmarks.measures: real repo bug-fixing, verified by the repo's own fail-to-pass tests
benchmarks.public_reference: No lab publishes DeepSWE numbers for these models. Dataset pinned at datacurve-ai/deep-swe@435ee89, 113 tasks.
caveats: Provenance is weaker than the recorded git SHA suggests. Every worker image in production is a stack of `docker commit` layers on a build from commit 863ddf1; the SHA label and BENCH_RUNNER_GIT_SHA env are written onto committed containers, not produced by a build at that commit. Verified separately: all 89 application .py files in the image hash-match the repo working tree exactly, so the code is the code the SHA names — but the image is not reproducible from it. Being repaired by locking the dependencies (an honest rebuild spent 45+ minutes in pip resolution, which is why commit-stacking became the habit).
One observation per cell. Within-cell spread on this harness has been measured up to 4x, so the token columns support no efficiency comparison and are shown as raw observations only.
Items 0 and 28 were chosen, not sampled. This is a paired head-to-head on two tasks, not an estimate of DeepSWE performance.

cells.notes: 1 of 2. Passed item 0 (20/20 fail-to-pass), failed item 28 at 136/137. Identical per-item outcome to vanilla Codex.
1 of 2. Same two outcomes as chutescoder, task for task. On this sample the harnesses tie.
0 of 2. Scored strictly below both Codex-derived arms on both items (19/20 and 124/137). This is the only comparison in which chutescoder leads.

mechanism_proof.$comment: Read from the retained evidence archives, from outside the sandbox. Every number here is in an artefact on disk whose sha256 is recorded in the database and was recomputed to match.
mechanism_proof.claim: The two arms are the same binary with one flag. The retained rollouts show the flag doing exactly what the design says: the RLM build reaches the host through a single `python` tool and never issues a shell call; the baseline issues only shell calls and never a `python` one.

arms.label: chutescoder (RLM on)
arms.note: One of four retained runs on this task. See `replication` — the score difference did not survive repetition; the tool-call invariant did.

arms.label: chutescoder-baseline (RLM off)
arms.note: One of four retained runs on this task. See `replication` — the score difference did not survive repetition; the tool-call invariant did.

mechanism_proof.archive_contents: MANIFEST.json, full rollout JSONL, effective config, model catalog, agent combined stdout/stderr, exit code, launch script (11 entries per archive)
what_it_does_not_show: It does not show the mechanism makes the agent better. Across every scored attempt at this one task the arms stand at 4/5 (RLM on) against 1/5 (RLM off) — Fisher's exact p = 0.206 two-tailed, which is what a real effect and a coin-flip both look like at n = 5.

This particular pair ran while two of my own diagnostic docker builds were pinning cores on the same host (load 5.05). Rollout CONTENT is unaffected by CPU contention, so the mechanism evidence stands; the scores and latencies from this pair are marked contaminated and are being re-run.
The fewer-turns observation (323 vs 479) is the shape the design predicts, but it is one pair. Within-cell spread on this harness has been measured up to 4x.

replication.$comment: Four retained pairs on the same task. Added after the initial pair, because repetition changed the conclusion.
replication.invariant_holds: RLM-on issues `python` and never a shell call; RLM-off issues shell calls and never `python`. 82 and 123 vs 114 and 117 — four for four, no exceptions. The mechanism claim rests on four artefacts.
replication.capability_collapsed: The score separation weakened at every single repetition: 2/2 vs 0/2 -> 3/4 vs 1/4 -> 4/5 vs 1/5 (p=0.206) -> 4/5 vs 2/6 (p=0.242) -> 4/6 vs 2/6 (p=0.567). On this task there is no capability difference we can demonstrate.
replication.turn_counts: chutescoder 323 (pass) and 485 (fail); baseline 479 (fail) and 601 (pass). Means 404 vs 540 — about a 25% turn reduction, not the 54% the single pass-to-pass pair suggested. Spread within the RLM-on arm alone is 162 lines. Recorded as a direction to test, not a finding.
